sources.title: H. B. Meyer, Lattice QCD: A Brief Introduction, in Lattice QCD for Nuclear Physics, Lecture Notes in Physics 889
sources.locator: §§1.2.3–1.2.4, printed pp. 11–14, and §1.4.1.1, pp. 22–24; the link transformation, traced-loop gauge invariance, Wilson plaquette action, Haar link integrals and strong-coupling expansion were read.

contents.name: Link variables and endpoint gauge transformation

source_review.supports: Eq. 1.57 gives the link endpoint transformation; §1.2.4 gives traced-loop invariance, plaquette holonomy and the lattice Wilson action.
source_review.limitations: The finite abstract two-complex, closedness proof, Haar probability existence and Gauss-sector closure are specified or proved locally.

contents.name: Gauge-invariant traced loops and plaquette action

source_review.supports: The trace of a closed Wilson line is unchanged by the endpoint similarity transformation; Eq. 1.64 gives the plaquette word and Eq. 1.66 the gauge action.
source_review.limitations: The proof here directly cancels the vertex factors and does not infer mathematical validity from the physical exposition.

contents.name: Haar integration and the leading strong-coupling surface term

source_review.supports: Eqs. 1.105–1.110 explain link Haar integration and the leading-order plaquette tiling mechanism.
source_review.limitations: The source is a four-dimensional leading-order expansion; it does not prove the exact finite two-dimensional SU(2) formula, which is derived locally.

sources.title: R. Lohmayer, Eigenvalue Distributions of Wilson Loops
sources.locator: §§3.5.2–3.5.5, printed pp. 44–51, and §§4.1–4.2.2, pp. 59–64; lattice Wilson loops, two-dimensional factorization, exact rectangular area law and the non-Abelian one-plaquette integral were read.

source_review.supports: The temporal-gauge change of variables factors the two-dimensional pure-gauge partition function into plaquette integrals.
source_review.limitations: The thesis uses an infinite lattice and temporal gauge; the local proof instead constructs a root-fixed spanning-tree gauge on the finite free-boundary rectangle.

contents.name: 4.2 Exact area law for Wilson loops

source_review.supports: The source derives the exact rectangular Wilson-loop area dependence from the one-plaquette matrix mean.
source_review.limitations: The exact finite-container SU(2) statement and the displayed positive coefficient are rederived from explicit local integrals.

source_review.supports: Group invariance reduces the one-plaquette matrix expectation to a scalar multiple of the identity, which motivates the matrix-average argument.
source_review.limitations: The source focuses on unitary groups and the Gross–Witten transition; the SU(2) round-measure integral and strict bounds are computed locally.

sources.title: H. B. Meyer, Lattice QCD: A Brief Introduction, in Lattice QCD for Nuclear Physics, Lecture Notes in Physics 889
sources.locator: §§1.2.4 and 1.4.1.1, printed pp. 13–14 and 22–24; the plaquette trace, Haar integration and leading Wilson-loop expansion were read.

contents.name: Single plaquette Wilson loop and Haar integration

source_review.read_extent: Complete §§1.2.4 and 1.4.1.1, printed pp. 13–14 and 22–24, inspected.
source_review.supports: The plaquette trace is a closed Wilson loop and the strong-coupling discussion uses normalized link Haar integrals.
source_review.limitations: The exact finite SU(2) one-face integral and its coefficient are established by the local proof.

contents.name: Two-plaquette tiling term in the leading expansion

source_review.supports: The leading minimal-surface expansion predicts the area power through plaquette tiling.
source_review.limitations: This is a leading-order four-dimensional illustration; the two-plaquette exact expectation follows from the finite two-dimensional theorem instead.

sources.title: R. Lohmayer, Eigenvalue Distributions of Wilson Loops
sources.locator: §§4.1–4.2.2, printed pp. 59–64; one-plaquette reduction and exact rectangular area dependence were read.

source_review.supports: The one-plaquette expectation supplies the scalar coefficient in the exact area formula.
source_review.limitations: The local example specializes the general integral to the explicit normalized round SU(2) measure.

source_review.supports: The exact area dependence yields the two-plaquette specialization with area two.
source_review.limitations: The thesis uses infinite-volume gauge fixing; this example uses the finite free-boundary theorem proved on the A page.
